This is the main AST-to-type conversion layer for paths, types, regions, and generic arguments. If elided return lifetimes are being accepted incorrectly during signature lowering, this is a prime place for the regression to have entered.

This file explicitly walks explicit and elided lifetime uses and tracks which binders are in scope for bare functions. That is exactly the machinery that can miscount the input lifetimes and let an elided return type slip through.

The shared lifetime-resolution results are stored here, including the resolved lifetime mapping and elision-related metadata. It is less likely to be the root cause than the lowering/collection code, but still sits on the critical path for this regression.

Late resolution handles lifetimes in bodies and records fallback lifetime resolutions. If the function signature was being normalized into an apparently valid lifetime shape, this resolver is a plausible upstream contributor.

The parser must accept the reference and lifetime syntax before later phases can decide whether elision is valid. It is a lower-probability candidate, but still part of the path for the reported signature.

This is the per-body type-checking context used for function and closure checking. It can propagate an incorrectly lowered signature into later type checking, making it a secondary suspect after the lifetime collection code.

The top-level checking coordinator wires together the item and body checking pipeline that consumes the lowered lifetime information. It is broader and less specific, but still on the path where the missing-lifetime error should ultimately be enforced.
